title: Normalized slice scalar adjunction and product Hom chain isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafification of sectionwise scalar extension and $U$ restriction of scalars, both applied termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $T(A)=S\otimes_R A$ for the underlying $R$-linear sheaf tensor, termwise. Write $H_R(P,J)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ and $H_S(K,N)=\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(K,N)$ for the actual product Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]; their local degree-$n$ sections have coordinates $f^i:P^i|_W\to J^{i+n}|_W$ on $\mathcal C/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. All pure tensors below mean their images under the tensor sheafification units [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and evaluation means the actual product projection followed by evaluation at the identity object of the slice.
For every object $W$, every $R|_W$-module sheaf $M$ and $S|_W$-module sheaf $L$, the assignments
$$g\longmapsto(x\mapsto g(1\otimes x)),\qquad h\longmapsto(s\otimes x\mapsto s h(x))$$
are mutually inverse additive bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{S|_W}(S|_W\otimes_{R|_W}M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R|_W}(M,UL)$, compatible with further slice restriction and pre- and postcomposition. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\nu_A:T(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}UEA$ sending $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes x$. For arbitrary $R$-complex $P$ and $S$-complex $N$ there is a natural $R$-linear chain isomorphism
$$\theta_{P,N}:U H_S(EP,N)\xrightarrow{\sim} H_R(P,UN),\qquad (\theta(g))^i(p)=g^i(1\otimes p),$$
whose inverse in degree $n$ sends a local family $(h^i)_i$ to the family of $S|_W$-linear sheaf maps $s\otimes p\mapsto s h^i(p)$. Here $d(f)^i=d_J f^i-(-1)^n f^{i+1}d_P$, and the asserted isomorphism commutes with this differential. Naturality of $\theta$ is contravariant in $P$ and covariant in $N$. No flatness, boundedness, finite-support, K-injectivity, or preservation of infinite products by $E$ is assumed.

proof.text: First identify scalar extension on slices with restriction of scalar extension. For $j_W:\mathcal C/W\to\mathcal C$, restriction is precomposition and the covering sieves over $V/W$ are exactly those over $V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Thus $j_W$ is continuous (restriction sends sheaves to sheaves), and cocontinuous: every covering sieve on $V$ lifts to the sieve with the same arrows, given their composite maps to $W$. Both sites are small in the stated module universe. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-slice-module-sheafification] to this functor and the ring sheaf $S$. The presheaves of tensors before sheafification are identical, since their value at $V/W$ is $S(V)\otimes_{R(V)}M(V)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Consequently there is a natural isomorphism $(EM)|_W\cong E_W(M|_W)$ taking the unit image of $s\otimes m$ to that same unit image. The comparison is normalized by its sheafification-unit transpose, as specified by the cited lemma. Restriction of scalars commutes with slice restriction sectionwise by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. These comparisons also apply to further slice restrictions.

source.place: Tags 03DH (section-localize), 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); explicit covering-sieve verification for slice restriction.

proof.text: On each small slice $\mathcal C/W$ apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] with the ring map $R|_W\to S|_W$. Its sheafification hypotheses hold by smallness, and the chosen $E_W$ is additive: for module maps $a,b$ one has $E_W(a+b)(s\otimes x)=s\otimes(a(x)+b(x))=E_Wa(s\otimes x)+E_Wb(s\otimes x)$, and uniqueness through sheafification extends the equality to sheaf maps. Its normalized Hom bijection is $g\mapsto(x\mapsto g(1\otimes x))$. To identify the inverse, let $h:M\to UL$. On every object of the slice the formula $(s,x)\mapsto s h(x)$ is additive in both variables and balanced, because $s h(rx)=s\varphi(r)h(x)$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives a linear map from the presheaf tensor. The equality $(s h(x))|_V=s|_V h(x|_V)$ makes these maps a presheaf map; it is $S$-linear since $(ts)h(x)=t(sh(x))$. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extends it uniquely to $E_WM\to L$. Its adjunct is $h$, since $1h(x)=h(x)$, so it is the inverse of the cited bijection. Alternatively the other composite is $s\otimes x\mapsto s g(1\otimes x)=g(s\otimes x)$; tensor generation and sheafification uniqueness make this the identity on all sections.

These slice bijections are additive and $R(W)$-linear: evaluating $g_1+g_2$ or $rg$ at $1\otimes x$ gives respectively $g_1(1\otimes x)+g_2(1\otimes x)$ or $r g(1\otimes x)$. Their inverses are additive and linear too, by bijectivity. For $a:M'\to M$, $b:L\to L'$ one has $(b\circ g\circ E_Wa)(1\otimes x)=b(g(1\otimes a(x)))$, proving both composition naturalities. Under further restriction $V\to W$, the unit comparison of step 1 sends $1\otimes x$ to $1\otimes x$; the two restricted forward maps therefore agree. The inverses agree by uniqueness of inverses. These are equalities of sheaf maps because they hold on every object of every slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. With the slice description and scalar action of [def-pur-sheaf-hom], the same formulas give isomorphisms of sheaves of $R$-modules, rather than merely bijections of global Hom sets.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and $W$. By [def-pur-hom-complex] the degree-$n$ sections of the source are the full product of $S|_W$-linear sheaf maps $(EP^i)|_W\to N^{i+n}|_W$, indexed by $i\in\mathbf Z$. Use the unit-normalized slice comparison of step 1 and apply the bijection of steps 2–3 separately in every coordinate. It gives $(\theta^n(g))^i(p)=g^i(1\otimes p)$ and inverse $(h^i)_i\mapsto(s\otimes p\mapsto s h^i(p))_i$. The two composites are the identity in every coordinate. Their compatibility with restrictions and $R(W)$-linearity, proved in step 3, make them inverse morphisms of $R$-module sheaves, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Restriction of scalars changes only the action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so the source product has exactly these same section families. This constructs the degreewise isomorphism using a product of bijections; it never applies $E$ to an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product terms; Tag 03CZ of sites-modules.tex on each coordinate.

proof.text:
Check the differential on an arbitrary further object $V\to W$ and $p\in P^i(V)$. Since $d_{EP}^i(1\otimes p)=1\otimes d_P^i(p)$, the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex] gives
$$\bigl(\theta^{n+1}(dg)\bigr)^i(p)=d_N^{i+n}\bigl(g^i(1\otimes p)\bigr)-(-1)^n g^{i+1}(1\otimes d_P^i(p))=\bigl(d\theta^n(g)\bigr)^i(p).$$
Equality for every $V,p,i$ is equality of the local sheaf maps and then of all product coordinates. Thus $\theta$ is a chain map. Its degreewise inverse is also a chain map: multiply $d\theta=\theta d$ by the inverses on both sides to obtain $d\theta^{-1}=\theta^{-1}d$. This proves the chain isomorphism with the exact sign convention in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), displayed differential; explicit evaluation calculation.

proof.text:
Finally let $a:P'\to P$ be an $R$-linear chain map and $b:N\to N'$ an $S$-linear chain map. The functoriality in [def-pur-hom-complex] is coordinatewise composition. On every slice its degree-$n$, coordinate-$i$ formula becomes
$$\theta_{P',N'}\bigl(b\circ g\circ Ea\bigr)^i(p)=b^{i+n}\bigl(g^i(1\otimes a^i(p))\bigr)=\bigl(b\circ\theta_{P,N}(g)\circ a\bigr)^i(p).$$
Together with the differential calculation this is naturality as chain maps, contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $N$; inverse naturality follows by cancellation. All constructions used arbitrary integer-indexed families, tensor universal properties and module sheafification. Consequently the result applies to the stated unbounded complexes without flatness or K-injectivity assumptions, and uses the actual slice evaluation at $V$ (in particular at the identity of each slice).
